records.brandNotes: The official Abarth Australia 500e page contains no numeric spec table, only navigation/offer links, so specs are sourced from carsales.com.au and CarSorted (secondary, medium confidence). CarExpert (25 Jul 2025) reported that global 500e production (the donor car for the Abarth 500e) was halted in 2024 amid slow sales, and Fiat's own offers page ('DRIVE AWAY FROM $43,990... while stocks last') plus a driveaway promotion reported by thebeep.com.au running 10 Jul 2025 to 30 Sep 2026 both point to clearance/run-out stock rather than an ongoing, freshly-produced model line; availability is therefore marked 'runout' for both variants rather than 'current'. Only 219 Scorpionissima units were allocated to Australia out of a global 1949-unit run, reinforcing the limited/run-out nature of that variant. AC charge rate could not be confirmed from any source and is left null.

records.brandNotes: GAC (Guangzhou Automobile Group) trades in Australia as 'GAC' with the 'AION' (also styled Aion) sub-brand used for its BEV models. GAC Australia launched in November 2025 with three models (Aion V BEV, Emzoom petrol SUV, M8 PHEV people-mover), then added the Aion UT BEV hatch in March/April 2026, confirmed via GAC's official en-au site (gacgroup.com.au/en-au), CarExpert, Drive, EV Central, carsales, and NRMA. GAC also displayed the Aion V and Aion UT alongside GAC-badged (non-Aion) PHEV/ICE models (M8 PHEV, Emzoom) at the 2026 Melbourne Motor Show; those non-BEV GAC models are out of scope for this file. As of Sept 2026 only two Aion nameplates are sold new/orderable in Australia: Aion V (mid-size SUV, on sale since Nov 2025) and Aion UT (compact hatch, on sale since March 2026). No Aion Y, Hyptec, or other Aion-badged BEV was found confirmed for the Australian market. Official GAC Australia site (gacgroup.com.au/en-au) currently (Sept 2026, within the Q3 2026 order window) advertises the Aion UT Premium at a national drive-away price of $31,990 for orders placed 1 Jul-30 Sep 2026; CarExpert/Drive/EV Central report the standing (non-promotional) RRP as $31,990 (Premium) / $35,990 (Luxury) before on-road costs, which is what is recorded here as priceAud/priceBasis, with the current drive-away promo noted separately. Aion V DC charge rate variously reported at up to 180kW; Aion UT DC charge rate variously reported (thebeep: 87kW; CarExpert reviews emphasise a 24-minute 30-80% fast charge without stating a peak kW figure) - recorded dcChargeKw for Aion UT is lower-confidence.

records.priceBasis: MSRP before on-road costs; national drive-away promotional price also advertised at $31,990 for Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) orders per official GAC Australia site

The Junior range is sold in Australia as both 'Ibrida' (petrol hybrid) and 'Elettrica' (BEV); the Ibrida is excluded entirely as it is not a BEV. Only one named Elettrica trim could be confirmed from the official site's spec block (115kW/260Nm, 54kWh, WLTP 407km); the multiple price points reported by CarExpert for 2026 ($58,990 before on-road costs base, with drive-away figures spanning $50,117-$64,057 and separately $60,813/$62,913/$64,057) most likely reflect colour and option-pack pricing rather than genuinely distinct named sub-variants, so a single Elettrica row is used rather than inventing separate trim names. DC fast-charge time is quoted as ~27 minutes (20-80%) on the official AU site vs ~30 minutes (10-80%) in a Stellantis press release; the official AU site figure is preferred.

Audi Australia is mid-transition from MY26 to MY27 pricing/lineups as of Sept 2026. Q8 e-tron / SQ8 e-tron is explicitly stated by Audi Australia as 'no longer available to order' and is excluded. A6 e-tron / S6 e-tron was reported cancelled for the Australian market (multiple AU motoring press, Nov 2025) and is excluded entirely. Q4 e-tron single-motor (150kW) variant pricing was announced by Audi Australia but detailed order/spec information had not been published at time of research, so most technical fields for that variant are null. Q6 e-tron/SQ6 e-tron technical figures (battery, power, torque, WLTP range) are sourced from Audi global technical data sheets (uploads.audi-mediacenter.com / emea-dam.audi.com) rather than an AU-specific spec page, and mapping of the exact WLTP range figure to each AU-market trim carries some uncertainty following Audi Australia's simplification to a 2-tier Q6 e-tron / SQ6 e-tron pricing structure for MY27; flagged via lowConfidenceFields. e-tron GT range figures were not able to be independently re-verified in this pass and are left null rather than guessed.

Official bmw.com.au model overview pages for i4/i5/i7/iX/iX3 (bmw.com.au/en/all-models/bmw-i/.../overview.html) repeatedly returned crawl timeouts and could not be read directly; data for those models is triangulated from BMW's electric-cars.html summary page plus the bmw.com/en-au (global CMS, AU locale) model pages, cross-checked against CarExpert's Australian pricing/spec database. iX1: BMW's own electric-cars.html lists 'iX1 eDrive20' but recent (Mar 2026) CarExpert/GoAuto pricing-change coverage and the 2026 iX3-era spec pages only describe a dual-motor xDrive30 (230kW/494Nm/64.8kWh) as the AWD-only variant sold in Australia; no independent confirmation of a currently-orderable eDrive20 was found, so eDrive20 is omitted rather than guessed. records.brandNotes: Cadillac Australia sells a single BEV model, the Lyriq (right-hand-drive, imported/converted by GM Specialty Vehicles). Battery capacity (102kWh) and AC/DC charging figures (11.5kW AC / 190kW DC) are consistent across sources and treated as reliable. However, pricing and power-output figures show real conflict: launch-era press (2024/early 2025) cited approx. $117,000-$122,000 drive-away for the Luxury variant, while later 2025/2026 secondary sources (dealer/aggregator listings) show substantially lower drive-away figures in the $90,000-$95,000 range, consistent with reported price cuts and a shift to a single-trim MY27 lineup. Power output is also inconsistently reported: 272kW (single-motor RWD figure per some specs) vs 388kW (dual-motor AWD figure per others), and it is not clear from available sources which figure corresponds to the actual current-model-year AU-market variant. Because these conflicts could not be reconciled with confidence, priceAud and powerKw are set to null and flagged low-confidence rather than guessing which figure is current.

records.brandNotes: Denza is BYD's premium sub-brand, sold new in Australia through its own showroom network (denza.com/au). Denza Australia's line-up as of Sept 2026 is: B5 and B8 (large PHEV off-road SUVs, launched late 2025 - out of scope, not BEV), D9 (electric 7-seat people-mover, on sale since March 2026 - BEV, in scope) and Z9GT (electric performance grand tourer/shooting-brake, confirmed for Australia and debuted at the April 2026 Melbourne Motor Show, with local deliveries reported for around September 2026). Multiple sources (CarExpert, TheBeep) explicitly confirm Australia skips the Chinese-market D9 PHEV entirely - every D9 sold locally is the 103.36kWh BEV, so both D9 variants below are BEV. The Z9GT is sold overseas in both BEV and PHEV ('DM') form, but Denza Australia has confirmed it is launching only the BEV Z9GT initially and is still 'evaluating' whether to bring the PHEV DM version to Australia - so the PHEV Z9GT is NOT in the Australian market and is excluded. As of the Sept 2026 fetch date, Australian pricing for the Z9GT had not yet been publicly confirmed (a CarExpert review dated 28 Aug 2026 states 'Australian pricing... has yet to be confirmed'), so priceAud is null and availability is recorded as 'announced' rather than 'current'. Z9GT range is reported inconsistently between an AU-specific CLTC claim (Denza Australia via CarExpert, 'no less than 1036km') and a Euro-spec WLTP claim (600km) in a later CarExpert quick-drive review of the Euro/pre-AU-launch car; the CLTC figure attributed directly to Denza Australia is used here and the WLTP conflict is flagged as low-confidence. DC charge rate caveat: the Z9GT's 1,500 kW figure is BYD's published FLASH Charging ceiling, achievable only on BYD's own China-market connector and charger. No Australian public charger can deliver it; on CCS2 infrastructure here the practical peak is far lower. Other sources quote 1,100 kW (evkx.net) for this pack and 270 kW for the 100 kWh Z9GT EV, so treat it as a platform claim rather than an Australian real-world rate.

records.brandNotes: Ford Australia currently sells BEVs only in its van/LCV range (E-Transit and E-Transit Custom). Ford has no BEV passenger car or SUV on sale in Australia in Sept 2026 (Mustang Mach-E was discontinued locally; no replacement confirmed). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: ford.com.au's 'future-vehicle/next-gen-e-transit-custom' page lists a Trend variant with a 45kWh usable battery, 160kW motor and 340km WLTP range, which conflicts with the currently-orderable E-Transit Custom Trend/Sport specs (64kWh usable battery, 301-307km WLTP) confirmed via Ford's own spec-sheet PDF and independent fleet press (Nov 2025). Because the ford.com.au URL is explicitly namespaced 'future-vehicle', the 45kWh/340km spec is treated here as an ANNOUNCED/NOT-YET-ON-SALE next-generation update rather than the current on-sale spec, and is excluded from variants below pending confirmation of on-sale date. Pricing for E-Transit Custom variants is sourced from a fleet trade publication (Nov 2025) rather than Ford's own price list, which was not directly accessible; flagged low-confidence. E-Transit (full-size van) pricing shows some inconsistency across secondary sources ($89,990 single figure vs a $89,990-$104,990 range for higher trims); only the base/entry configuration is captured with confidence. V2L CORRECTION (Sept 2026): both E-Transit Custom variants were previously reconciled with inconsistent v2l values (Trend null, Sport true) sourced from a generic aggregator (evdbau.com). A dedicated Australian first-drive review (The Driven, Nov 2025) explicitly states Ford chose not to fit V2L to the E-Transit Custom in Australia, across both trims; both variants are now set to v2l:false accordingly. The full-size E-Transit (420L)'s V2L status could not be confirmed either way in this pass and is left null rather than guessed.

records.brandNotes: IM Motors (also known as Zhiji / IM Presented by MG) is confirmed in the Australian market. The brand is a premium EV sub-brand of SAIC, sold through the MG Motor Australia dealer network (110+ dealers). The IM5 sedan and IM6 SUV first entered Australia in mid-2025 (sources cite June or July 2025), with a major formal launch event on 30 July 2026 at Sydney's White Bay Cruise Terminal. Large-scale customer deliveries began in early September 2026. The brand uses the trading name 'IM Presented by MG' in Australia. Pricing has shifted since the June 2025 launch: launch prices were $60,990/$69,990/$80,990 drive-away; thebeep.com.au (as of September 2026) shows $57,990/$64,990/$74,990 drive-away reflecting subsequent price reductions confirmed by EOFY promotions. All prices recorded here are from thebeep.com.au as most current. The official spec sheet (MG_IM6_Specs_v8.pdf) from mgmotor.com.au is used for detailed technical specifications. Neither the IM5 nor IM6 has yet received an ANCAP star rating as of September 2026; testing has been submitted. No IM8 or other IM models confirmed for AU as of this date.

Pricing has fluctuated heavily via promotions (as low as $40,000 drive-away in early 2026 vs an original before-on-road-costs launch price of $53,990); the $49,990/$54,990 before-on-road-costs figures used here are the most recent 'before on-road costs' figures reported by CarExpert (March 2026). records.brandNotes: LDV's only current-generation electric ute (eT60) is included with reasonably solid figures. The eT60's successor, the eTerron 9 (Maxus eTerron 9 globally), has been repeatedly delayed since an original 'early 2025' target; as of Aug 2026 press coverage LDV Australia says it 'continues to work with the factory' with no confirmed on-sale date, so it is EXCLUDED from variants per the 'omit anything not confirmed for Australia' rule (see notes for spec preview). eDeliver 7 pricing is highly inconsistent across sources: LDV's own site advertises a promotional drive-away price for MY23 SWB Low Roof ($54,990 driveaway, ABN-holder offer ending 30 Sept 2026), while CarExpert's 2026 pricing tool shows a base drive-away price of $46,305-$48,411 for one configuration and a wider drive-away band of $61,042-$82,009 across ~12 listed configurations that appear to mix diesel and electric drivetrains inconsistently in the underlying data. Given this inconsistency, eDeliver 7 priceAud is set to null and flagged low-confidence; only body/battery/range specs believed reliable are included. eDeliver 9 pricing and specs are consistent across CarExpert (2022-2023) and LDV's own site and are treated as higher-confidence, though the RRP figures originate from a 2023 launch report un-updated for potential 2026 changes. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): a CarsGuide reviewer's Australian eDeliver 7 test drive explicitly states 'a big disappointment is the lack of V2L or an internal three-pin outlet', so v2l is set to false for both eDeliver 7 variants (flagged low-confidence: single-reviewer source). No V2L feature is mentioned anywhere on LDV Australia's own eDeliver 9 page or in CarExpert's/CarsGuide's eDeliver 9 coverage, consistent with the eDeliver 7 finding for the same manufacturer/generation, so v2l is set to false there too (flagged low-confidence: absence-of-evidence rather than an explicit manufacturer denial). eT60 (Sept 2026 pass): CarExpert's Australian review explicitly wishes for 'a Ford-style vehicle-to-load (V2L) system' to be added, confirming it is not fitted; the ute does have 12V and 220V interior sockets, but that is not full V2L. No later coverage through the 2026 model year indicates this has changed, so v2l is set to false with medium confidence.

Mercedes-Benz Australia's own model pages rarely publish full technical-data tables or pricing in a scrapeable form (most figures are rendered via JS widgets), so most numeric specs below had to be corroborated via AU motoring press (CarExpert, carsales, Chasing Cars, WhichCar, carsorted.ai, evdrives.com.au, electriccaradviceaustralia.com.au, cartell.tv). Where sources conflicted I selected the figure from the source that appeared most internally consistent and flagged the field as low-confidence; unresolved conflicts are called out per-variant below. EQC is confirmed discontinued in Australia (orders closed 2023, no longer listed as a current model family by CarExpert as of 2026) and is excluded. The updated EQS sedan (800V architecture, up to 925km WLTP) is confirmed for Australian launch in Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec) but pricing/final AU spec was still unconfirmed as of the April 2026 CarExpert report, so those four variants are marked availability=announced with null pricing; the current EQS450 4MATIC and AMG EQS53 4MATIC+ sedans remain the orderable current-generation variants until that changeover. The Mercedes-AMG EQE SUV 53 4MATIC+ is confirmed to exist on the AU site but no numeric specs or pricing could be verified, so most fields are null. Full-electric AMG models (EQE53, EQS53, Maybach EQS680) are genuine BEVs and are included; mild-hybrid AMG/EQ Boost ICE models are excluded per task scope.

The base entry-level 'Cooper E' and 'Aceman E' (lower-power, smaller-battery, single-motor FWD variants below SE) were discontinued in Australia in early 2025 (CarExpert, Jan 2025: 'Mini killing off its cheapest EVs in Australia', production ended March 2025) and, per CarExpert's Jan 2026 pricing article, remain unavailable as new orders in 2026 ('the entry-level electric Cooper E is currently unavailable'). They are therefore omitted here rather than guessed at. Mini's official pages consistently quote a 'usable' battery figure (49.2kWh for Cooper/Aceman, ~64.8-65.2kWh for Countryman) that is lower than the 'maximum'/gross figure surfaced by CarExpert's spec database (54.2kWh and 66.5kWh respectively); both figures are included as batteryUsableKwh/batteryGrossKwh based on this mapping, but the mapping itself (which article is 'usable' vs 'gross') is inferred rather than explicitly labelled as such on a single page, so it is flagged low-confidence throughout. The official mini.com.au Countryman page text extracted for this research showed older 432-462km WLTP range figures; more recent CarExpert (Aug 2026) and manufacturer running-change coverage (Jun 2026) confirm updated SiC-inverter range and pricing figures (up to 501km/467km WLTP, revised pricing, and deletion of the entry 'Countryman E Core' trim), which are used here in preference to the older cached figures. No BEV Mini model other than Cooper, Aceman and Countryman was found to be sold or announced for Australia.

The Performance pack for Polestar 2 and 3 requires Plus pack to be ordered concurrently and is treated here as a distinct variant following Polestar's own spec-page structure. Polestar 3 Dual motor and Performance variant prices could not be confirmed for MY2026 specifically and are set to null. The Polestar 4 coupé (windowless) is the current orderable body; the Polestar 4 SUV (with rear window, MY2027) is announced for late 2026 delivery but not yet confirmed orderable as of September 2026 and is therefore excluded. V2L not offered on any current Polestar AU models per brand policy (not mentioned on any AU product page). Polestar 2 body is a 5-door fastback; 'hatch' is the closest schema value. Consumption figures are WLTP ranges (not a single number) — set to null.

records.brandNotes: V2L (Sept 2026 pass): no V2L/V2X capability found for the EC11 in any manufacturer or press material reviewed (importer spec sheet, CarsGuide, AEVA-derived light-commercial fact sheet summaries); v2l set to false for both E-Cargo and E-Crew and flagged low-confidence given the sparse documentation for this independently-imported model. Skywell IS genuinely sold new in Australia, but only as a single model, the EC11 electric van (in E-Cargo and E-Crew body variants), imported and distributed by an independent Australian importer, EV Automotive (ev-a.com.au), rather than by a Skywell-badged factory-backed distributor. This is corroborated by multiple independent commercial channels: fleetplan.com.au and easifleet.com.au both list the EC11 as a current new/novated-lease vehicle in 2026, and carsales.com.au / carsguide.com.au / drive.com.au all carry EC11 research/showroom pages. No other Skywell model (e.g. BE11, EV9, ET5) was found confirmed as on sale new in Australia as of Sept 2026 - the EC11 is the only current Skywell nameplate in market. Pricing is genuinely unclear/unverifiable: Drive.com.au's showroom page lists a 2025 E-Cargo RWD at $59,990 (MRLP, GST-inclusive, excl. on-roads), while CarsGuide cites third-party (Glass's Information Services) pricing of $89,990-$120,000 for the 2026 range, and carsales.com.au's own research pages say price is simply 'not available' for both the E-Cargo and E-Crew. EV Automotive's own official site (ev-a.com.au) does not publish a price at all. Given this scale of disagreement across sources (a >$30k spread) and the complete absence of a price on the importer's own site, priceAud is recorded as null for both variants rather than guessed. Technical specifications for the E-Cargo variant are well documented on ev-a.com.au's own specification table and are used directly; the E-Crew (12-seat people-mover) variant shares the same underlying platform/powertrain per Drive.com.au and BitAuto but EV Automotive's site does not carry a dedicated detailed spec sheet for it, so several E-Crew fields are recorded as null pending a dedicated spec page.

smart is confirmed actively sold in Australia as of September 2026 via the official au.smart.com site, which lists two current model lines: smart #1 and smart #3 (both Geely-Mercedes-Benz-joint-venture BEVs), each with three trims (Pro+, Premium, BRABUS). smart #1 data below was extracted directly from the official smart.com/au configurator/model pages (primary source). smart #3 official model page did not expose a full technical-data table in scrapeable form, so smart #3 specs are corroborated from AU motoring press (carsorted.ai, CarExpert, carsales) and are lower confidence overall. Two systematic gaps: (1) the smart #1 official page states 200kW only for the Premium trim and 315kW for BRABUS, without repeating the figure for Pro+; real-world knowledge suggests Pro+ shares Premium's powertrain, but per the no-invention rule this is left null and flagged rather than assumed. (2) Battery usable capacity for smart #3 could not be confirmed on any AU source reviewed; left null. Pricing for smart #1 is the official RRP before on-road costs; pricing for smart #3 is sourced from press (some of which quote drive-away pricing rather than MSRP) and is flagged accordingly. Torque figures for higher-power / dual-motor variants (smart #1 BRABUS, smart #3 BRABUS) are ambiguous in sources (single motor vs combined system torque are not always distinguished) and are flagged low-confidence or left null rather than risk conflating a single-motor spec with a combined system figure.

records.priceBasis: MSRP before on-road costs (VW AU list price, per CarExpert/Drive reporting)
records.brandNotes: Only BEV models in current AU lineup are ID.4, ID.5 and ID.Buzz (incl. ID.Buzz Cargo commercial van). ID.3 and ID.7 are NOT sold in Australia (ID.7 has been repeatedly ruled out by VW Australia spokespeople in press statements from 2023 through 2026, citing focus on the electric SUV range). VW Australia's own model pages predominantly advertise driveaway campaign pricing rather than MSRP before on-road costs; priceAud below uses the manufacturer list price (before on-road costs) as reported in VW's own price-cut announcements and corroborated by CarExpert/GoAuto/CarsGuide, per each variant's priceBasis field. Several ID.Buzz technical figures (GTX torque: 590Nm per CarExpert vs 560Nm per CarsGuide; Pro LWB power: 210kW assumed vs a conflicting 120kW figure in one CarsGuide table; AC charge rate assumed at VW's standard 11kW where not separately confirmed; towing capacity for ID.5 assumed identical to the equivalent-drivetrain ID.4 per AEVA, and largely unpublished for ID.Buzz Pro/GTX variants) show conflicts across secondary sources or were not published by VW Australia at all; these are flagged per-variant in lowConfidenceFields. VW's AEVA fact sheet confirms the ID.4 (and by extension the MEB-based ID.5) has no V2X/V2L capability in the Australian market, despite one aggregator (evdbau) claiming V2L support for the ID.5 -- the AEVA figure was preferred as the more EV-specialist, dated source. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): all four ID.Buzz variants (same MEB platform as ID.4/ID.5) previously had v2l left null; VW Commercial Vehicles has announced a 2.0kW V2L function arriving via a 'Summer 2026' software update, but reporting is explicit that this rollout is currently Europe/UK-only with no confirmed Australian timing, so the current AU-market ID.Buzz (incl. Cargo) is set to v2l:false, flagged low-confidence pending confirmation of if/when the update reaches Australia.

Community-sourced ev-wiki.org mentions of an 'ES90' for Volvo Australia was NOT corroborated by any official or reputable press source and has been excluded entirely rather than included as a speculative row. EX40 (the renamed XC40 Recharge — previously wrongly excluded from this file as an unconfirmed 'community-sourced' claim; it is in fact a genuine, currently-sold model) has now been added. Its /specifications/ sub-page returned 403 at fetch time, so EX40 figures below are press-sourced (CarExpert, thebeep) rather than manufacturer-confirmed, and are flagged low-confidence accordingly. Press sources disagreed materially on price by ~$5,000-13,000 depending on state/promo/drive-away timing; the figures used here come from CarExpert's 2026-03-31 report of a $7,000 national MSRP price cut, which is the most specific and recent single data point found. PRICE AND SPEC CORRECTIONS (Sept 2026 pass): volvocars.com.au's own /specifications/ pages for EX30 and EX90 return 403 to automated fetches (Volvo's own bot-blocking, not a client-side network/VPN issue — confirmed by retrying after ruling out a local Cloudflare WARP/DNS cause), so this pass is press-sourced. EX30 priceAud filled from CarExpert's dedicated Plus/Ultra spec pages and its EX30 Cross Country pricing article, which gives a clean one-page table of all four current EX30 configurations. EX90 priceAud filled from a Chasing Cars review giving both Plus ($124,990) and Ultra Performance ($134,990) prices with matching power/torque figures. While researching EX90 pricing, multiple independent sources (CarsGuide's own Plus Twin Motor spec page, thebeep.com.au, Chasing Cars, general press) consistently gave power/torque/range/0-100 figures materially different from what this file previously recorded (300kW/770Nm/5.9s for Twin Motor vs the previous 330kW/670Nm/5.5s; 380kW/910Nm/4.9s for Twin Motor Performance vs the previous 500kW/870Nm/4.2s; 570km WLTP for both vs the previous 521km) — these look like a genuine prior data error rather than a source disagreement, since every current source agrees with each other and disagrees with the old figures, so they have been corrected rather than left as a documented conflict. EX30's existing power/torque/battery/range figures were re-checked against CarExpert's dedicated Plus/Ultra spec pages during this pass and found to match exactly (200kW/343Nm/69kWh gross/64kWh usable/462km WLTP for Single Motor Extended Range), so those fields were left unchanged.

records.brandNotes: XPENG launched in Australia in late 2024 via distributor TrueEV. Factory-backed XPeng ANZ (XPeng Australia and New Zealand) took over distribution in April 2026; TrueEV and XPeng are in Federal Court proceedings. XPeng ANZ is currently selling: (1) the updated G6 (referred to as 'New G6' or 2027 MY in some press, arriving in AU showrooms July 2026) in four variants; and (2) the X9 electric people mover (available to order July 2026, deliveries commencing shortly after). While the X9 is sold as an EREV in China, Australia receives BEV-only versions — no EREV exclusion required for X9. The L03 BEV and G9L BEV are confirmed for AU launch in Q4 2026 (October–December) but not yet orderable as of September 2026; they are included as 'announced'. The L03 also has an EREV version; only BEV is listed here. The G9L will offer both EV and EREV in AU; only BEV listed. The L05 is scheduled for January 2027 and is not included. Note: the xpeng.com.au/g6-specification page as indexed appears to show the outgoing 2024 G6 (190 kW, 66 kWh, 435 km WLTP); the current 'New G6' specs are sourced from the store.xpeng.com/au configurator. Towing capacity for G6 and X9 is not confirmed in AU specifications reviewed. G6 segment is 'suv-small' per GoAuto press categorisation ('Small SUV over $45K segment').

records.brandNotes: Zeekr is firmly established in Australia as of September 2026 with three BEV model lines: Zeekr X (small SUV), Zeekr 7X (medium SUV), and Zeekr 009 (people-mover/MPV). All are orderable through the Zeekr Australia dealer network. The 2026 Zeekr X launched in Australian showrooms from May 2026 with national drive-away pricing. The 7X has been on sale since 2025. The 009 FWD grade was added in November 2025. The 8X and 9X announced for late 2026/early 2027 are PHEV/EREV (not BEV) and are therefore excluded from this file. The 7GT electric wagon was mentioned as under consideration for AU launch but is not confirmed as orderable and is excluded. Prices for the 7X are drive-away from thebeep.com.au (aggregated from Zeekr Australia); 009 prices are before on-road costs per Drive.com.au. VFACTS/EVC sales data confirms real AU volumes: Zeekr X 665 total 2025 sales, 142 YTD 2026; Zeekr 009 123 total 2025 sales, 97 YTD 2026; Zeekr 7X 2,698 units Jan-Apr 2026.
