brands.notes: The official Abarth Australia 500e page contains no numeric spec table, only navigation/offer links, so specs are sourced from carsales.com.au and CarSorted (secondary, medium confidence). CarExpert (25 Jul 2025) reported that global 500e production (the donor car for the Abarth 500e) was halted in 2024 amid slow sales, and Fiat's own offers page ('DRIVE AWAY FROM $43,990... while stocks last') plus a driveaway promotion reported by thebeep.com.au running 10 Jul 2025 to 30 Sep 2026 both point to clearance/run-out stock rather than an ongoing, freshly-produced model line; availability is therefore marked 'runout' for both variants rather than 'current'. Only 219 Scorpionissima units were allocated to Australia out of a global 1949-unit run, reinforcing the limited/run-out nature of that variant. AC charge rate could not be confirmed from any source and is left null.

brands.publisher: GAC International Australia (GAC Group, en-au site)
brands.notes: GAC (Guangzhou Automobile Group) trades in Australia as 'GAC' with the 'AION' (also styled Aion) sub-brand used for its BEV models. GAC Australia launched in November 2025 with three models (Aion V BEV, Emzoom petrol SUV, M8 PHEV people-mover), then added the Aion UT BEV hatch in March/April 2026, confirmed via GAC's official en-au site (gacgroup.com.au/en-au), CarExpert, Drive, EV Central, carsales, and NRMA. GAC also displayed the Aion V and Aion UT alongside GAC-badged (non-Aion) PHEV/ICE models (M8 PHEV, Emzoom) at the 2026 Melbourne Motor Show; those non-BEV GAC models are out of scope for this file. As of Sept 2026 only two Aion nameplates are sold new/orderable in Australia: Aion V (mid-size SUV, on sale since Nov 2025) and Aion UT (compact hatch, on sale since March 2026). No Aion Y, Hyptec, or other Aion-badged BEV was found confirmed for the Australian market. Official GAC Australia site (gacgroup.com.au/en-au) currently (Sept 2026, within the Q3 2026 order window) advertises the Aion UT Premium at a national drive-away price of $31,990 for orders placed 1 Jul-30 Sep 2026; CarExpert/Drive/EV Central report the standing (non-promotional) RRP as $31,990 (Premium) / $35,990 (Luxury) before on-road costs, which is what is recorded here as priceAud/priceBasis, with the current drive-away promo noted separately. Aion V DC charge rate variously reported at up to 180kW; Aion UT DC charge rate variously reported (thebeep: 87kW; CarExpert reviews emphasise a 24-minute 30-80% fast charge without stating a peak kW figure) - recorded dcChargeKw for Aion UT is lower-confidence.

The Junior range is sold in Australia as both 'Ibrida' (petrol hybrid) and 'Elettrica' (BEV); the Ibrida is excluded entirely as it is not a BEV. Only one named Elettrica trim could be confirmed from the official site's spec block (115kW/260Nm, 54kWh, WLTP 407km); the multiple price points reported by CarExpert for 2026 ($58,990 before on-road costs base, with drive-away figures spanning $50,117-$64,057 and separately $60,813/$62,913/$64,057) most likely reflect colour and option-pack pricing rather than genuinely distinct named sub-variants, so a single Elettrica row is used rather than inventing separate trim names. DC fast-charge time is quoted as ~27 minutes (20-80%) on the official AU site vs ~30 minutes (10-80%) in a Stellantis press release; the official AU site figure is preferred.

Audi Australia is mid-transition from MY26 to MY27 pricing/lineups as of Sept 2026. Q8 e-tron / SQ8 e-tron is explicitly stated by Audi Australia as 'no longer available to order' and is excluded. A6 e-tron / S6 e-tron was reported cancelled for the Australian market (multiple AU motoring press, Nov 2025) and is excluded entirely. Q4 e-tron single-motor (150kW) variant pricing was announced by Audi Australia but detailed order/spec information had not been published at time of research, so most technical fields for that variant are null. Q6 e-tron/SQ6 e-tron technical figures (battery, power, torque, WLTP range) are sourced from Audi global technical data sheets (uploads.audi-mediacenter.com / emea-dam.audi.com) rather than an AU-specific spec page, and mapping of the exact WLTP range figure to each AU-market trim carries some uncertainty following Audi Australia's simplification to a 2-tier Q6 e-tron / SQ6 e-tron pricing structure for MY27; flagged via lowConfidenceFields. e-tron GT range figures were not able to be independently re-verified in this pass and are left null rather than guessed.

Official bmw.com.au model overview pages for i4/i5/i7/iX/iX3 (bmw.com.au/en/all-models/bmw-i/.../overview.html) repeatedly returned crawl timeouts and could not be read directly; data for those models is triangulated from BMW's electric-cars.html summary page plus the bmw.com/en-au (global CMS, AU locale) model pages, cross-checked against CarExpert's Australian pricing/spec database. iX1: BMW's own electric-cars.html lists 'iX1 eDrive20' but recent (Mar 2026) CarExpert/GoAuto pricing-change coverage and the 2026 iX3-era spec pages only describe a dual-motor xDrive30 (230kW/494Nm/64.8kWh) as the AWD-only variant sold in Australia; no independent confirmation of a currently-orderable eDrive20 was found, so eDrive20 is omitted rather than guessed. A next-generation (U11) iX1 xDrive30 is confirmed by bmw.com/en-au for an 11/2026 Australian launch but its page showed only placeholder/blank spec values as of the fetch date, so it is NOT included here (not yet orderable with verifiable specs); treat the current-gen iX1 xDrive30 entry below as the model orderable today. iX3: two model generations are on sale/announced in AU during 2026 - the existing iX3 50 xDrive (current, on bmw.com.au's headline EV list) and an iX3 40 RWD variant reported by CarExpert (Aug 2026) as launching in Q4 2026 ('by year's end') - as of 13 Sep 2026 this is marked 'announced' rather than 'current' since it is not yet listed on BMW's own current EV lineup page and deliveries had not been reported as started. i4: the range was cut to a single eDrive35 grade in Oct 2025 (Drive.com.au); the previous eDrive40 and M50 grades are no longer sold in Australia and are omitted. i7: BMW's Australian pricing for xDrive60/M70 is inconsistently reported across secondary sources (RRP vs Sydney drive-away estimates differ by roughly $5k-$15k); priceAud below uses the figure most consistent with an ex-on-road MSRP framing, flagged low-confidence. No 'iXM' BEV nameplate could be verified as an existing or announced Australian BMW model (BMW's XM is a PHEV, not a BEV) so it has been omitted entirely, per the 'do not invent' rule.

BYD AU model-specific pages failed to load via ExaContents and browser URL guesses. All pricing and most specs sourced from CarExpert AU and Drive.com.au as secondary sources; brand website (byd.com/au) confirmed model lineup only. Sealion 6 (PHEV) and Shark 6 (PHEV ute) excluded — both have petrol engines. Atto 3 transitioning to Evo nameplate Sept 2026; pre-Evo Essential listed as runout (leftover stock per CarExpert Aug 2026). Dolphin AC/DC charging rates not confirmed in any source reviewed — set to null. V2L confirmed for Atto 3 Evo variants only. Seal and Sealion 7 V2L not confirmed — set to null. Towing capacity not found for Dolphin and Sealion 7. Atto 1 added 2026-09-15: Essential grade corroborated across three press outlets (Chasing Cars, CarsGuide, Drive.com.au) reporting a $19,990 national drive-away promotional price (standard MSRP $23,990 before on-road costs, no stated offer end date); Premium grade specs come from a single aggregator (thebeep.com.au) only and are flagged low-confidence. 2026-09-21: confirmed V2L for both Atto 1 grades and 11kW AC charging for Premium via bydautomotive.com.au/atto-1 (official BYD AU page, previously unreachable). Atto 1 Essential AC/DC charge rates and Premium DC charge rate and towing still not found.

Cadillac Australia sells a single BEV model, the Lyriq (right-hand-drive, imported/converted by GM Specialty Vehicles). Battery capacity (102kWh) and AC/DC charging figures (11.5kW AC / 190kW DC) are consistent across sources and treated as reliable. However, pricing and power-output figures show real conflict: launch-era press (2024/early 2025) cited approx. $117,000-$122,000 drive-away for the Luxury variant, while later 2025/2026 secondary sources (dealer/aggregator listings) show substantially lower drive-away figures in the $90,000-$95,000 range, consistent with reported price cuts and a shift to a single-trim MY27 lineup. Power output is also inconsistently reported: 272kW (single-motor RWD figure per some specs) vs 388kW (dual-motor AWD figure per others), and it is not clear from available sources which figure corresponds to the actual current-model-year AU-market variant. Because these conflicts could not be reconciled with confidence, priceAud and powerKw are set to null and flagged low-confidence rather than guessing which figure is current.

Chery (as distinct from Omoda/Jaecoo) sells exactly one BEV model in Australia: the Chery E5, currently one variant (Ultimate) after the entry-level Urban trim was discontinued for MY26. The Chery eQ7 is NOT sold in Australia - it is a China-domestic CLTC-rated model with no AU dealer presence, ADR compliance, or pricing; excluded. Chery's remaining AU lineup (Tiggo 4/7/8/9, C5) is petrol, HEV or PHEV ('Super Hybrid') and is excluded. Chery AU publishes only a driveaway price for the E5 ($37,990, valid 1 Jul-30 Sep 2026); no separate before-on-road-costs MSRP is brand-published. Brand's own spec sheet does not distinguish usable vs gross battery capacity (58.9kWh single figure). Braked towing capacity is not published by Chery; only an unbraked 750kg figure exists. V2L is reported as false per an AEVA technical note stating the E5 does not currently include V2X capability.

WITHDRAWN FROM MARKET: Citroen Australia (importer Inchcape) formally ceased all new-vehicle sales in Australia effective 1 November 2024, ending a 101+ year presence, after sales collapsed to just 87 units in H1 2024 (down 35% year-on-year, versus a 2007 peak of 3803 annual deliveries). Existing orders placed before 1 November 2024 were fulfilled, and Citroen's ~35 dealer network transitioned to a service-and-maintenance-only operation; the importer refocused on its sibling brand Peugeot. At the time of withdrawal Citroen's Australian range was petrol/diesel only (C3, C4, C5 Aircross, C5 X) -- no BEV was part of the final local lineup. Search results also surfaced ccarprice.com listings claiming current Australian availability and pricing for an e-C4 X, e-Berlingo and e-SpaceTourer; ccarprice.com is a low-reliability, seemingly auto-generated aggregator that explicitly disclaims guaranteed accuracy, and its claims directly conflict with the official Citroen Australia market-exit announcement and multiple corroborating reputable press sources (carsales, WhichCar, Drive, CarExpert), so those listings are treated as incorrect/not credible and excluded. As of September 2026, Citroen sells no new vehicles of any powertrain in Australia, BEV or otherwise.

Cupra's only currently orderable BEV in Australia is the Tavascan (SUV/coupe-SUV on VW Group's MEB platform). The Cupra Born (electric hatch) is NOT currently orderable: the official cupraofficial.com.au/cars/born page states 'Currently unavailable to order in Australia. Now sold out.' as of this Sept 2026 fetch, so it is excluded from variants per the orderable-now criterion. The live-scraped official Tavascan page shows 'TWO CUPRA TAVASCAN VARIANTS' (Endurance and VZ), but a third, cheaper 'V' variant (RWD, LFP battery, lower power/range) is corroborated by multiple 2026 Australian press sources (CarExpert, evcentral.com.au, carsales.com.au, GoAuto) reporting a MY26 range update that added an entry-level V grade and revised Endurance/VZ range and pricing. Because this V variant and the MY26 Endurance/VZ figures are not confirmed by a fresh read of the official brand page itself, all three variants carry lowConfidenceFields flags on the affected fields (mainly range, price and availability), with press URLs cited via fieldSources. AC charge rate (11kW) is assumed at VW Group's standard onboard charger rate, not separately confirmed per variant, and is flagged low-confidence throughout. V2L capability is not confirmed by any source sighted for any Tavascan variant, so it is recorded as null rather than guessed.

IMPORTANT EREV EXCLUSION: Deepal sells S07 and L07 globally in both pure-BEV and EREV (range-extender) form. In Australia only the S07 is sold, and only as a pure BEV - no EREV S07 has launched here. The L07 sedan has NOT launched in Australia at all (official L07 AU page returns 404 as of this research; AU press describes it only as teased/under consideration since Oct 2024, no confirmed date or pricing) - excluded entirely, not listed as announced due to lack of any confirmed AU launch commitment. Deepal E07 'Multitruck' is a BEV; its EREV version exists only in China and is unconfirmed for AU - excluded. E07 is a 5-seat SUV-ute crossover, included here as a passenger vehicle per Deepal/AU press classification (not a dual-cab ute). S07 19-inch-wheel variant is sold out (runout); only the 20-inch variant remains orderable. Deepal AU has moved to drive-away-only promotional pricing for S07 as of Sept 2026; the E07 prices below are stated as MSRP/MLP before on-road costs per WhichCar/CarExpert. No official usable-vs-gross battery split is published for either model.

Denza is BYD's premium sub-brand, sold new in Australia through its own showroom network (denza.com/au). Denza Australia's line-up as of Sept 2026 is: B5 and B8 (large PHEV off-road SUVs, launched late 2025 - out of scope, not BEV), D9 (electric 7-seat people-mover, on sale since March 2026 - BEV, in scope) and Z9GT (electric performance grand tourer/shooting-brake, confirmed for Australia and debuted at the April 2026 Melbourne Motor Show, with local deliveries reported for around September 2026). Multiple sources (CarExpert, TheBeep) explicitly confirm Australia skips the Chinese-market D9 PHEV entirely - every D9 sold locally is the 103.36kWh BEV, so both D9 variants below are BEV. The Z9GT is sold overseas in both BEV and PHEV ('DM') form, but Denza Australia has confirmed it is launching only the BEV Z9GT initially and is still 'evaluating' whether to bring the PHEV DM version to Australia - so the PHEV Z9GT is NOT in the Australian market and is excluded. As of the Sept 2026 fetch date, Australian pricing for the Z9GT had not yet been publicly confirmed (a CarExpert review dated 28 Aug 2026 states 'Australian pricing... has yet to be confirmed'), so priceAud is null and availability is recorded as 'announced' rather than 'current'. Z9GT range is reported inconsistently between an AU-specific CLTC claim (Denza Australia via CarExpert, 'no less than 1036km') and a Euro-spec WLTP claim (600km) in a later CarExpert quick-drive review of the Euro/pre-AU-launch car; the CLTC figure attributed directly to Denza Australia is used here and the WLTP conflict is flagged as low-confidence. DC charge rate caveat: the Z9GT's 1,500 kW figure is BYD's published FLASH Charging ceiling, achievable only on BYD's own China-market connector and charger. No Australian public charger can deliver it; on CCS2 infrastructure here the practical peak is far lower. Other sources quote 1,100 kW (evkx.net) for this pack and 270 kW for the 100 kWh Z9GT EV, so treat it as a platform claim rather than an Australian real-world rate.

Farizon Auto (a Geely-group commercial vehicle brand) has launched electric vans in Australia: the SV 'SuperVan' range (SWB/LWB, low/high roof configurations) and the V7E van (Standard/Extended Range). The Farizon H9E was identified in sourcing as a 'Light Truck' model; its GVM could not be confirmed against the 4.5-tonne inclusion threshold used in this dataset, so it has been excluded pending verification rather than guessed into or out of scope. Sept 2026 pass: previously both SV and V7E were recorded with almost all fields null pending confirmation; this pass fills in SV SWB Low Roof and both V7E trims from converging AU press coverage (CarsGuide's Australian first-drive review for SV; carsales.com.au, trucksales.com.au and a Farizon dealer blog for V7E, all reporting the same 50kWh/66kWh battery, 110kW/230Nm and $49,990/$53,990 drive-away figures). V2L is confirmed standard on both models: CarsGuide's SV review states it supports vehicle-to-load 'through Australian domestic household plugs at up to 3.3kW of continuous power' (though the reviewer noted it did not work on their test unit); V7E's V2L is confirmed as a standard feature across three independent sources (trucksales.com.au, carsales.com.au, and a Farizon dealer blog) though none states a wattage figure for it. Farizon's own SV LWB and LWB High Roof configurations are known to exist (per press coverage) but no Australian pricing/specs could be confirmed for them in this pass, so they remain excluded rather than guessed.

The official fiat.com.au 500e page contains only marketing copy ('discover pricing' / 'book a test drive'), not a numeric spec table, so battery/power/range figures are sourced from secondary press (CarSorted aggregator + CarExpert), flagged medium confidence. CarExpert (25 Jul 2025) reported that global production of the standard 500e was halted in 2024 amid slow sales, with a hybrid version in development for production from late 2025; this casts real doubt on ongoing new-vehicle availability of the BEV 500e in Australia by September 2026, so availability is marked 'runout' rather than 'current'. Steep drive-away discounting (down to $38,990 drive-away vs $52,500 before-ORC RRP, an offer that ran only to 30 September 2025) is consistent with stock clearance. Only one current trim, 'La Prima', was confirmed; a separate 'Icon' trim was referenced only in an ANCAP test-vehicle description on CarExpert and could not be confirmed as a distinct orderable Australian trim, so it is not listed as a separate row.

Ford Australia currently sells BEVs only in its van/LCV range (E-Transit and E-Transit Custom). Ford has no BEV passenger car or SUV on sale in Australia in Sept 2026 (Mustang Mach-E was discontinued locally; no replacement confirmed). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: ford.com.au's 'future-vehicle/next-gen-e-transit-custom' page lists a Trend variant with a 45kWh usable battery, 160kW motor and 340km WLTP range, which conflicts with the currently-orderable E-Transit Custom Trend/Sport specs (64kWh usable battery, 301-307km WLTP) confirmed via Ford's own spec-sheet PDF and independent fleet press (Nov 2025). Because the ford.com.au URL is explicitly namespaced 'future-vehicle', the 45kWh/340km spec is treated here as an ANNOUNCED/NOT-YET-ON-SALE next-generation update rather than the current on-sale spec, and is excluded from variants below pending confirmation of on-sale date. Pricing for E-Transit Custom variants is sourced from a fleet trade publication (Nov 2025) rather than Ford's own price list, which was not directly accessible; flagged low-confidence. E-Transit (full-size van) pricing shows some inconsistency across secondary sources ($89,990 single figure vs a $89,990-$104,990 range for higher trims); only the base/entry configuration is captured with confidence. V2L CORRECTION (Sept 2026): both E-Transit Custom variants were previously reconciled with inconsistent v2l values (Trend null, Sport true) sourced from a generic aggregator (evdbau.com). A dedicated Australian first-drive review (The Driven, Nov 2025) explicitly states Ford chose not to fit V2L to the E-Transit Custom in Australia, across both trims; both variants are now set to v2l:false accordingly. The full-size E-Transit (420L)'s V2L status could not be confirmed either way in this pass and is left null rather than guessed.

Foton's current Australian passenger/light-commercial lineup (Tunland V7 and Tunland V9 utes, priced approx. $39,990-$49,990) is confirmed across multiple 2025/2026 sources to be diesel or diesel mild-hybrid only, with no battery-electric variant offered new in Australia. No evidence was found this session of an on-sale Foton or Foton-affiliated (e.g. 'Asiastar') BEV in the Australian market; a prior research pass had flagged a possible 'Tunland G7 EV' but this could not be corroborated this session against any dealer, press, or manufacturer source and is treated as unconfirmed/likely incorrect. Foton does sell electric light trucks/buses in some overseas markets, but none were verified as available for retail new-vehicle purchase in Australia within the 4.5-tonne GVM passenger/LCV scope of this dataset.

Fuso's eCanter range spans multiple GVM classes from 4.5 tonnes up to 8.55 tonnes. Per this dataset's scope rule excluding vehicles above 4.5 tonne GVM, only the smallest variant (e515 City Cab, 4.5t GVM) is included; all higher-GVM eCanter variants (6.0t, 7.49t, 8.55t) are excluded as out of scope. Fuso does not publish a retail RRP for the eCanter: the vehicle is explicitly marketed as 'available for lease' with pricing varying per customer/fleet agreement, so priceAud is null. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): the eCanter has no V2X capability in the Australian market (Fuso's own AU FAQ page makes no mention of it); a home/emergency-power V2X function does exist for the Japanese domestic market only and is not offered here, so v2l is set to false and flagged low-confidence.

GWM's only currently orderable BEV in Australia is the Ora 5 SUV (Lux, Ultra). The original Ora hatch (Good Cat/Funky Cat) was discontinued around April/May 2026, superseded by the Ora 5; not included as it is no longer sellable as new stock. An Ora 5 Hatch and Ora 5 Touring (wagon, larger battery) have been referenced by AU press as coming 'later in 2026' but are unconfirmed/no specs - excluded pending confirmation. Haval Jolion Max BEV is a confirmed future AU launch targeting Q4 2026 but is not yet orderable and has no official specs published - excluded (announced only, insufficient verified data to list). GWM's ute range (Cannon, Cannon Alpha, Cannon Hi4-T) is diesel/PHEV only - no BEV ute exists in the AU lineup. No BEV van exists in the GWM/Ora/Haval AU range. GWM AU publishes drive-away pricing only; no official MSRP-before-on-roads figure exists (the pre-on-road figures below are back-calculated by CarExpert, medium confidence). Range cycle is WLTC per the brand site and AU press, not WLTP - recorded as null for rangeCycle since WLTC is not one of the permitted enum values, with the true value noted in fieldSources/notes per variant.

Geely Australia currently sells three models: EX2 (BEV hatch), EX5 (BEV SUV), and Starray EM-i (PHEV, 1.5L petrol + battery - excluded, not a BEV). No Geely EX7, Preface, Monjaro, Emgrand or Galaxy Cruiser are on sale yet; these are announced/under consideration for 2026-2027 but not orderable, and excluded pending confirmation. EX5 received a battery/range update in 2026 (68.39kWh, up from an earlier 60.22kWh pack); the exact new kWh figure is sourced only from Drive.com.au (medium confidence) since geely.com.au itself does not publish the number, only range/performance claims - flagged. Both EX5 variants are explicitly stated by Geely/AEVA as not rated for towing (0kg), reported here as 0 rather than null since it is an explicit manufacturer statement. Pricing is RRP/MSRP before on-road costs as stated by geely.com.au, not driveaway.

GV60 Advanced spec confirmed directly from Genesis Australia's official brochure PDF - a major mid-2026 change replaced the previous dual-motor AWD entry model with a cheaper single-motor RWD 'Advanced' grade. The performance GV60 Magma has not had pricing announced. Electrified G80 battery capacity (94.5kWh) and WLTP range are confirmed directly from the official genesis.com.au electric/charging page, which supersedes an outdated 87.2kWh figure found on ev-wiki.org for a prior model year. Electrified GV70 could not be confirmed via a direct genesis.com.au fetch in this research pass; pricing is sourced from CarSorted (AU-specific aggregator) and battery/range from ev-wiki.org, both secondary sources, so most numeric fields for GV70 are marked low confidence. US-market Genesis figures (Edmunds/KBB) were deliberately excluded as AU-spec vehicles differ.

The Honda Super-ONE is Honda's first BEV for the Australian market, a Kei-class city car sold initially via an Expression of Interest (EOI)/pre-order process rather than a standard dealer order book; treated as 'current' since pricing and specs are confirmed and pre-orders are open. Range-cycle conflict: Honda's own EOI page states 'up to 253km range (NEDC)' while GoAuto's August 2026 pricing-confirmation article (citing Honda's own final pricing announcement) states a WLTP range of 206km for the same car - these are not the same test cycle and are recorded separately rather than merged; the more recent WLTP 206km figure accompanying final pricing is used as the primary rangeKm/rangeCycle, with the NEDC 253km figure noted as a low-confidence alternate in fieldSources. Power rating is dual-mode: 47kW standard, up to 70kW/162Nm in 'BOOST Mode' (a temporary boost via a simulated 7-speed transmission) - powerKw records the peak 70kW boost figure per common EV convention, with the 47kW continuous rating flagged as an alternate in notes.

Kona Electric, Elexio, Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 5 N pricing/specs cross-checked across CarExpert and Chasing Cars 2026 pricing articles (before on-road cost MSRP). Ioniq 9 specs/pricing sourced from evdbau.com aggregator (medium confidence, AU-specific but not an official Hyundai page). Ioniq 6 status is genuinely uncertain as of Sept 2026: press aggregators (evdbau.com, ev-wiki.org) indicate the current Dynamiq/Techniq/Epiq range may be superseded/in transition ahead of a facelift and an upcoming Ioniq 6 N, with no single authoritative current price confirmed in this research pass. Ioniq 6 is therefore included with availability marked 'runout' and price left null rather than guessed; the facelift/N variants are not included as they are not confirmed orderable in AU as of this date.

brands.publisher: MG Motor Australia (mgmotor.com.au/vehicles/im6), CarSorted.ai, thebeep.com.au, zecar.com
brands.notes: IM Motors (also known as Zhiji / IM Presented by MG) is confirmed in the Australian market. The brand is a premium EV sub-brand of SAIC, sold through the MG Motor Australia dealer network (110+ dealers). The IM5 sedan and IM6 SUV first entered Australia in mid-2025 (sources cite June or July 2025), with a major formal launch event on 30 July 2026 at Sydney's White Bay Cruise Terminal. Large-scale customer deliveries began in early September 2026. The brand uses the trading name 'IM Presented by MG' in Australia. Pricing has shifted since the June 2025 launch: launch prices were $60,990/$69,990/$80,990 drive-away; thebeep.com.au (as of September 2026) shows $57,990/$64,990/$74,990 drive-away reflecting subsequent price reductions confirmed by EOFY promotions. All prices recorded here are from thebeep.com.au as most current. The official spec sheet (MG_IM6_Specs_v8.pdf) from mgmotor.com.au is used for detailed technical specifications. Neither the IM5 nor IM6 has yet received an ANCAP star rating as of September 2026; testing has been submitted. No IM8 or other IM models confirmed for AU as of this date.

Isuzu does not currently sell a battery-electric vehicle in Australia as of September 2026. The Isuzu D-Max EV (battery-electric dual-cab ute) has been confirmed by Isuzu as planned for the Australian market, and has appeared in various global/regional launches, but multiple 2025 reports indicate no confirmed Australian on-sale date, with local timing reportedly linked to New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES) policy settings and light commercial vehicle CO2 targets. No Isuzu BEV is currently orderable new in Australia.

REAL DOUBT / LIKELY WITHDRAWN: Jaguar's I-Pace was, as of a November 2024 review, sellable in Australia on remaining stock only ('sufficient stock... to carry us through to 2025'), following JLR's July 2024 global decision to axe the I-Pace and E-Pace as 'zero-profitability products'. CarExpert's own 2026 I-Pace pricing page (published 20 Aug 2026) shows 'Price not available' and zero year-to-date sales for 2026, and the official jaguar.com/en-au I-Pace specifications page itself returned a broken/unavailable content block at fetch time. Given no confirmed current price, zero 2026 sales, and a global discontinuation decision from mid-2024, the I-Pace is judged to be effectively no longer orderable new in Australia as of September 2026 and is therefore NOT listed as a current variant (an empty variants array is used) rather than assumed still on sale. Note also: a March 2026 CarExpert report described a recall affecting ~270 older (2017-2021 build) I-Pace units for a battery overheating/fire risk, capping charging at 90% pending a permanent fix -- this affects existing fleet vehicles, not new-vehicle orderability, and is unrelated to the withdrawal finding above. No other Jaguar BEV (e.g. a Jaguar 'Type 00' successor GT) has been confirmed as launched or orderable in Australia.

The Avenger is currently Jeep Australia's only BEV; it is sold exclusively as a front-drive EV locally (overseas petrol/mild-hybrid/4xe Avenger variants are not sold in Australia). WLTP range is quoted by the official jeep.com.au site as 'up to 390km'; a Stellantis press release separately cited 391-396km depending on trim, a minor discrepancy resolved in favour of the official AU site figure. Pricing has fluctuated heavily via promotions (as low as $40,000 drive-away in early 2026 vs an original before-on-road-costs launch price of $53,990); the $49,990/$54,990 before-on-road-costs figures used here are the most recent 'before on-road costs' figures reported by CarExpert (March 2026). Summit trim price could not be reconfirmed for 2026 (last known figure was $60,990 from September 2024) and is left null rather than guessed. IMPORTANT WITHDRAWAL: per EV Central (6 July 2026), Jeep has cancelled right-hand-drive production of both the Wagoneer S (flagship electric SUV, previously slated for Australian launch in 2026) and the Recon for markets including Australia and the UK, citing RHD development cost and market conditions; Jeep is instead pursuing a joint venture with Dongfeng for a future RHD-market SUV, targeted no earlier than late 2027. Neither Wagoneer S nor Recon is listed in variants as a result.

SsangYong has rebranded to KGM in Australia; kgm.com.au is the current official storefront. Only two BEV nameplates exist in the AU lineup: Torres EVX (SUV, single trim) and Musso EV (ute, 3 variants). The Actyon is confirmed hybrid/petrol only in Australia - no BEV Actyon exists; excluded. Korando e-Motion was never sold in Australia; excluded. KGM AU publishes drive-away pricing only; no official MSRP-before-on-roads figure exists (before-on-road figures are CarExpert back-calculations, medium confidence). Battery capacity (80.6kWh) is never split into usable vs gross by KGM for either model. 0-100km/h acceleration is not officially published by KGM for either model; low-confidence secondary figures exist but are not corroborated and are excluded from the main fields. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): confirmed high-confidence for all Musso EV variants -- CarExpert's Australian review states the Musso EV supports V2L at up to 3.5kW (15A) via an adaptor on the charge port; added as fieldSources citation (was previously uncited despite already being recorded as true).

EV5 data is high-confidence, sourced from Kia's official MY26 brochure PDF and AU offers page (drive-away pricing only). EV6 pricing/specs sourced from a detailed CarExpert article on the facelifted MY26 range because Kia's own AU offer pages for EV6 returned 404 errors when fetched directly. EV9 could not be confirmed against an official Kia AU page in this pass; specs are sourced from ev-wiki.org/thebeep.com.au aggregator data and are lower confidence, and MY26 pricing was not confirmed so priceAud is left null for all EV9 variants rather than guessed. PV5 Cargo added Sept 2026: Kia Australia's electric van (built on the new PBV platform) launched in market from May 2026 as a single 'Cargo S Long Range' configuration ($55,990 before on-road costs); specs are high-confidence, corroborated across CarExpert's Australian first-drive review, RACV and Chasing Cars. V2L is confirmed standard, with both an exterior V2L adaptor and an interior outlet in the cargo area, rated up to 3.68kW/3.6kW.

LDV's only current-generation electric ute (eT60) is included with reasonably solid figures. The eT60's successor, the eTerron 9 (Maxus eTerron 9 globally), has been repeatedly delayed since an original 'early 2025' target; as of Aug 2026 press coverage LDV Australia says it 'continues to work with the factory' with no confirmed on-sale date, so it is EXCLUDED from variants per the 'omit anything not confirmed for Australia' rule (see notes for spec preview). eDeliver 7 pricing is highly inconsistent across sources: LDV's own site advertises a promotional drive-away price for MY23 SWB Low Roof ($54,990 driveaway, ABN-holder offer ending 30 Sept 2026), while CarExpert's 2026 pricing tool shows a base drive-away price of $46,305-$48,411 for one configuration and a wider drive-away band of $61,042-$82,009 across ~12 listed configurations that appear to mix diesel and electric drivetrains inconsistently in the underlying data. Given this inconsistency, eDeliver 7 priceAud is set to null and flagged low-confidence; only body/battery/range specs believed reliable are included. eDeliver 9 pricing and specs are consistent across CarExpert (2022-2023) and LDV's own site and are treated as higher-confidence, though the RRP figures originate from a 2023 launch report un-updated for potential 2026 changes. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): a CarsGuide reviewer's Australian eDeliver 7 test drive explicitly states 'a big disappointment is the lack of V2L or an internal three-pin outlet', so v2l is set to false for both eDeliver 7 variants (flagged low-confidence: single-reviewer source). No V2L feature is mentioned anywhere on LDV Australia's own eDeliver 9 page or in CarExpert's/CarsGuide's eDeliver 9 coverage, consistent with the eDeliver 7 finding for the same manufacturer/generation, so v2l is set to false there too (flagged low-confidence: absence-of-evidence rather than an explicit manufacturer denial). eT60 (Sept 2026 pass): CarExpert's Australian review explicitly wishes for 'a Ford-style vehicle-to-load (V2L) system' to be added, confirming it is not fitted; the ute does have 12V and 220V interior sockets, but that is not full V2L. No later coverage through the 2026 model year indicates this has changed, so v2l is set to false with medium confidence.

Leapmotor launched in Australia in 2024 via its Stellantis distribution partnership. As of September 2026 the brand sells three distinct BEV model lines: the B10 small SUV (2 BEV variants), the C10 medium SUV (2 BEV variants), and the B05 small hatchback. EXCLUDED (non-BEV): the B10 Hybrid EV (EREV/range-extender, launched mid-2026 from $37,888 excl. ORC), the C10 Hybrid EV (EREV, launched 2025; known as 'Hybrid EV' locally, it is a range-extender plug-in hybrid with claimed total range ~1,150 km). Neither EREV variant is a BEV and both are omitted. The B05 is confirmed for AU (five-star ANCAP rating announced August 2026, priced from $35,990 driveaway) but only driveaway pricing is currently confirmed; pre-ORC MSRP and full technical specifications were not verified in sources reviewed and several fields are null. The C10 Style retains the older 400V architecture and 6.6 kW AC charging; the MY26 C10 Design LR upgraded to 800V with 11 kW AC and 180 kW DC. Towing for the C10 Style (1,500 kg braked) is confirmed via Carsales spec data; towing for the C10 Design LR (MY26) and B10 variants has not been separately confirmed for the 2026 spec and is marked as low confidence where populated. The official Leapmotor Australia website (leapmotor.net) returned minimal indexable content; specifications have been sourced from Carsales, CarExpert, Zecar, and CarSorted (which states it sources from the Leapmotor AU website).

RZ range confirmed via Lexus Australia's own press-room release plus a detailed CarExpert breakdown of the updated (price-reduced) MY26 range. The UX300e was discontinued in Australia (confirmed May 2025) and is not included. The RZ600e F Sport Performance flagship has been announced but is not yet priced/orderable, so it is included with availability 'announced' and technical fields null where not confirmed for AU. Steer-by-wire yoke and Toyota/Lexus DIRECT4 AWD equipment details are noted but not part of the schema.

Precise official trim names for the three Eletre and three Emeya power/price tiers could not be fully confirmed from the official site content retrieved; 'Eletre'/'Eletre S'/'Eletre R' and 'Emeya'/'Emeya S'/'Emeya R' are used based on the confirmed Emeya trim names (which ARE officially confirmed) applied by analogy to Eletre's three price/power tiers reported by thebeep.com.au (secondary, medium confidence) -- flagged low-confidence on variant naming for Eletre. Emeya power output is reported as 405kW by multiple secondary sources (manofmany.com, evdrives.com.au) for the Emeya/Emeya S, but CarExpert's overview page separately cited 450kW, which appears to be a copy-paste error from the Eletre spec block; 405kW is used here as the better-corroborated figure, flagged low-confidence. A warranty-term discrepancy exists between sources (5yr/150,000km reported for Eletre vs 3yr unlimited km reported for Emeya) but warranty is not a schema field so it is only noted here, not resolved. Eletre AC/DC charge rate figures could not be found in any source and are left null.

MG's current AU BEV range (per CarExpert, Sept 2026): MG4 EV Urban and MG4 EV hatchbacks, MGS5 EV and MGS6 EV SUVs, and the Cyberster roadster. MG ZS EV (and ZST) have been discontinued and are no longer sold as separate current models in Australia and are excluded here. MG U9 is confirmed for a future electric ute variant but is not yet on sale in Australia (petrol/diesel U9 currently sold) and is excluded as unconfirmed/not-yet-orderable. IMPORTANT: MG Motor Australia's own retail network also sells the IM5 and IM6 (badged 'IM' / built by IM Motors, a SAIC joint venture) alongside MG-badged EVs, and MG's own marketing sometimes describes its 'seven EVs on sale' as including IM5/IM6. Those two models are treated as the separate 'IM Motors' brand for this task and are NOT included in this file (see im-motors.json) to avoid double-counting. Most current pricing found on mgmotor.com.au is expressed as drive-away (not MSRP before on-road costs); where only drive-away price could be found this is noted in priceBasis and flagged in lowConfidenceFields. MG4 EV Urban Essence 54 price was reported as 'TBC' in press at time of writing and could not be confirmed, so priceAud is null.

Mahindra Australia sells ZERO battery-electric vehicles as of September 2026. The current retail lineup is exclusively internal-combustion: Scorpio (diesel), XUV3XO (petrol), XUV700 (petrol/diesel), plus an upcoming diesel-only Lifestyler dual-cab ute - none of these are electrified. AU press (carsales.com.au, 2026-09-02; Drive.com.au, 2026-09-02; GoAuto, 2026-08-18) reports Mahindra is evaluating a trio of EVs (XEV 9e, XEV 9S, BE 6) for possible future Australian launch - a single XEV 9e demonstrator has been imported on temporary plates for internal dealer display, and Australian trademark filings exist for 'XEV 9E' and 'BE 6' - but none has a confirmed launch date, Australian specification, or pricing. This does not meet the bar for 'announced' status (which requires a confirmed AU launch), so no variants are listed. Revisit this brand as these EVs progress toward a firm Australian launch commitment.

Official maserati.com/au spec pages returned only navigation elements (driveaway price calculator, stock locator, dealer finder) with no numeric spec table content retrievable, so battery capacity, range, torque, 0-100 time, AC/DC charge rates and seat count could NOT be confirmed for either model and are left null rather than guessed -- this is the largest data gap of any brand researched. GranTurismo Folgore pricing is confusing across sources: CarExpert's 2026 pricing-history table shows drive-away prices of $395,753-$474,618 for '2024' model-year cars, while a separate 2025-launch article and a dedicated spec page both cite '$450,000' as the 'before on-road costs' base price; $450,000 is used here as the MSRP figure since it is explicitly described as a before-on-road-costs base price, but the drive-away table figures should not be assumed equivalent. Grecale Folgore drive-away price citations were inconsistent ($122,763-$226,493 across different CarExpert table rows); the $207,500 before-on-road-costs figure is used as it was the only figure explicitly described as a base 'before on-road costs' price.

Mazda's previous BEV, the MX-30, was discontinued in Australia in 2023. The Mazda 6e liftback is Mazda's first mainstream BEV for Australia, confirmed directly via Mazda Australia's official model page and press-and-pricing release; first customer deliveries began July 2026, so by the September 2026 reference date the 6e is orderable/on sale and marked 'current'. Torque is quoted as 290Nm on Mazda's own official pricing release and by CarExpert/GoAuto, but carsales.com.au and an RACV review both cite 320Nm for the same 190kW motor - kept at the official 290Nm figure with the conflicting number flagged low confidence. Mazda's China-built EREV (extended-range/hybrid) variants of the 6e/CX-6e are explicitly excluded, as Mazda has confirmed they will not be sold in Australia - only the pure-BEV drivetrain is in scope. The CX-6e SUV twin was reported 'due Q3 2026' but no AU pricing, specs, or confirmed on-sale date were found in this research pass, so it is included as 'announced' with all technical fields null rather than guessed.

V2L (Sept 2026 pass): the EQV 300's V2L status could not be confirmed with a single quotable AU review (CHOICE gates its spec table behind membership, and several review sites returned no mention of the feature at all), but multiple independent searches converge on 'no V2L/V2G/V2H' for this model, consistent with it predating Mercedes' EQ V2L rollout on newer platforms; v2l set to false and flagged low-confidence pending a stronger citation. Mercedes-Benz Australia's own model pages rarely publish full technical-data tables or pricing in a scrapeable form (most figures are rendered via JS widgets), so most numeric specs below had to be corroborated via AU motoring press (CarExpert, carsales, Chasing Cars, WhichCar, carsorted.ai, evdrives.com.au, electriccaradviceaustralia.com.au, cartell.tv). Secondary sources frequently disagree with each other on price and range for the same variant (e.g. EQE300 quoted at both $135,200 and $149,900 before on-roads; EQE trims all showing an identical 571km WLTP figure on carsorted.ai, which looks like a templating bug). Where sources conflicted I selected the figure from the source that appeared most internally consistent and flagged the field as low-confidence; unresolved conflicts are called out per-variant below. EQC is confirmed discontinued in Australia (orders closed 2023, no longer listed as a current model family by CarExpert as of 2026) and is excluded. The updated EQS sedan (800V architecture, up to 925km WLTP) is confirmed for Australian launch in Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec) but pricing/final AU spec was still unconfirmed as of the April 2026 CarExpert report, so those four variants are marked availability=announced with null pricing; the current EQS450 4MATIC and AMG EQS53 4MATIC+ sedans remain the orderable current-generation variants until that changeover. For the EQS SUV range, sources disagree on whether the standard EQS450/EQS580 4MATIC SUV grades are still sold in Australia alongside the Maybach models as of 2026 (cartell.tv says yes, three AWD grades plus Maybach; a 2026 CarExpert model page states only 2 variants remain, both Maybach) - both are represented below with the standard grades flagged low-confidence; verify directly with Mercedes-Benz Australia before relying on this for the standard EQS SUV grades. The Mercedes-AMG EQE SUV 53 4MATIC+ is confirmed to exist on the AU site but no numeric specs or pricing could be verified, so most fields are null. Full-electric AMG models (EQE53, EQS53, Maybach EQS680) are genuine BEVs and are included; mild-hybrid AMG/EQ Boost ICE models are excluded per task scope.

The base entry-level 'Cooper E' and 'Aceman E' (lower-power, smaller-battery, single-motor FWD variants below SE) were discontinued in Australia in early 2025 (CarExpert, Jan 2025: 'Mini killing off its cheapest EVs in Australia', production ended March 2025) and, per CarExpert's Jan 2026 pricing article, remain unavailable as new orders in 2026 ('the entry-level electric Cooper E is currently unavailable'). They are therefore omitted here rather than guessed at. Mini's official pages consistently quote a 'usable' battery figure (49.2kWh for Cooper/Aceman, ~64.8-65.2kWh for Countryman) that is lower than the 'maximum'/gross figure surfaced by CarExpert's spec database (54.2kWh and 66.5kWh respectively); both figures are included as batteryUsableKwh/batteryGrossKwh based on this mapping, but the mapping itself (which article is 'usable' vs 'gross') is inferred rather than explicitly labelled as such on a single page, so it is flagged low-confidence throughout. The official mini.com.au Countryman page text extracted for this research showed older 432-462km WLTP range figures; more recent CarExpert (Aug 2026) and manufacturer running-change coverage (Jun 2026) confirm updated SiC-inverter range and pricing figures (up to 501km/467km WLTP, revised pricing, and deletion of the entry 'Countryman E Core' trim), which are used here in preference to the older cached figures. No BEV Mini model other than Cooper, Aceman and Countryman was found to be sold or announced for Australia.

Mitsubishi currently sells no BEV in Australia (the outgoing eK X EV kei car and i-MiEV were never sold locally, and the Outlander/Eclipse Cross PHEVs are plug-in hybrids, out of scope). The ASX VR-e - Mitsubishi's first BEV confirmed for Australia, built by Foxtron/Foxconn in Taiwan on the 'Foxtron Bria' platform under an OEM arrangement - has been confirmed via Mitsubishi Motors Corporation's own global press release and corroborated by GoAuto/CarExpert for a Q4 2026 Australian launch, with four variant names (LS, Aspire, Exceed, GSR) confirmed. However, as of this September 2026 research date no technical specifications (battery, power, range, charging) or pricing have been released for the Australian market, so all such fields are left null rather than guessed; availability is marked 'announced' since it is a confirmed future AU launch, not yet orderable.

Nissan Leaf: 2026 sales data (0 YTD) plus confirmed indefinite delay of the next-generation Leaf SUV, combined with confirmation that Sunderland production ceased, indicates the current Leaf is being sold through remaining stock only in Australia; marked availability 'runout'. Battery capacity figures for Leaf (40kWh/62kWh) are well-established industry-standard figures for this generation but were not re-confirmed against a fresh primary source in this research pass, so flagged low confidence. Nissan Ariya pricing is the official MSRP (before on-road costs) announced at July 2025 order-opening; a driveaway estimate was also seen in April 2026 press but the before-on-road figures are used here for consistency with the schema's priceBasis convention.

As of September 2026 the Omoda Jaecoo brand family sells exactly one BEV: the Jaecoo J5 EV, single grade 'Summit'. No BEV is currently sold under the Omoda badge - the model formerly marketed as 'Omoda E5' has reverted to the Chery brand name (now 'Chery E5', see chery.json) and is out of scope here. The Jaecoo J6 EV is NOT confirmed for Australia; Chery Australia has said it is 'under consideration' with no confirmed plans, and third-party pricing sites listing J6 AU pricing appear to be unreliable/auto-generated - excluded. Jaecoo J7 SHS (hybrid) and other hybrid/PHEV Jaecoo/Omoda models (Omoda 9 SHS-P) are excluded as non-BEV. Braked towing capacity is not published for the J5 EV (only an unbraked 750kg + 75kg towball figure exists).

e-2008 numeric specs (50kWh battery, 100kW/260Nm, WLTP 328km, $59,990) are from its 2023 Australian launch article (CarExpert) since the current official site page returned only navigation/comparison content, not a spec table; treated as medium confidence pending re-confirmation that these figures still apply unchanged in 2026. Peugeot's official electric van page still actively promotes e-Partner and e-Expert (including an e-Expert cashback offer running to 31 July 2026), confirming both remain currently orderable. e-Partner's official page does not publish a battery/power/range spec table (only payload/towing/dimensions), so those fields are null. An all-electric E-408 sedan/wagon has been discussed by Peugeot Australia as under consideration for the market but was NOT confirmed as launched or orderable, so it is excluded entirely per the instruction to omit anything not confirmed for Australia. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): neither Peugeot's own e-Partner page nor an EV Central range-test review of the Australian e-Partner mention any V2L/vehicle-to-load feature, despite Peugeot marketing V2L on other (EMP2-platform) electric models; v2l set to false and flagged low-confidence. e-Expert's V2L status could not be confirmed either way (its MY23 spec-sheet PDF was unreachable) and is left null rather than guessed.

Polestar AU does not publish standalone MSRP before on-road costs on public pages; instead uses MRDP (Manufacturer's Recommended Driveaway Price). Prices listed here are drive-away estimates from CarExpert.com.au (Sydney-based; include delivery, rego, plates, road taxes but not CTP or dealer fees) used as proxy for MRDP. The Performance pack for Polestar 2 and 3 requires Plus pack to be ordered concurrently and is treated here as a distinct variant following Polestar's own spec-page structure. Polestar 3 Dual motor and Performance variant prices could not be confirmed for MY2026 specifically and are set to null. The Polestar 4 coupé (windowless) is the current orderable body; the Polestar 4 SUV (with rear window, MY2027) is announced for late 2026 delivery but not yet confirmed orderable as of September 2026 and is therefore excluded. V2L not offered on any current Polestar AU models per brand policy (not mentioned on any AU product page). Polestar 2 body is a 5-door fastback; 'hatch' is the closest schema value. Consumption figures are WLTP ranges (not a single number) — set to null.

Porsche Australia confirms the Taycan Sport Turismo body style is NOT sold locally (Porsche Cars Australia spokesperson quoted by CarExpert, Aug 2024, reaffirmed by the current official body-type toggle on porsche.com/australia which shows only 'Sports Sedan' and 'Cross Turismo'), so it is excluded. The 11-model 'Sports Sedan' lineup and 3-model 'Cross Turismo' lineup below match the official Porsche Australia site's stated variant counts. Pricing (MRLP, excl. on-road costs) is sourced from drive.com.au, a secondary AU motoring-data source, because it explicitly labels its figures 'MRLP Excl. On-Roads' (matching this project's priceBasis requirement) — flagged via fieldSources/lowConfidenceFields on priceAud. Power figures for 4S and above are Porsche's official 'Overboost Power with Launch Control' ratings from the AU site; some third-party sources (e.g. drive.com.au spec pages) report a lower base/continuous power figure for the same variant, so powerKw and torqueNm carry some ambiguity and are flagged low-confidence. Battery capacity (gross/net kWh) and per-variant WLTP range for Taycan were not able to be confirmed variant-by-variant from an AU-specific official source in this pass; left null except for base Taycan/Taycan 4/Black Edition (Performance Battery), sourced from a global Porsche technical PDF, and flagged low-confidence. Macan Electric specs and pricing are corroborated by both the official Porsche Australia model pages (range figures) and carsorted.ai, a secondary aggregator that states it sources from the Porsche Australia website, giving higher confidence than the Taycan figures.

Ram does not currently sell any battery-electric vehicle in Australia as of September 2026. The Ram 1500 REV, a planned full-BEV version of the Ram 1500, was cancelled by Stellantis/RAM globally in September 2025 before reaching an Australian right-hand-drive conversion or launch. The Ram Ramcharger (an extended-range electric vehicle / EREV with a petrol generator providing extended range) is out of scope for this dataset because it is not a pure battery-electric vehicle. No other Ram BEV model is confirmed for the Australian market.

Megane E-Tech Techno EV60 specs/price sourced primarily from electriccaradvice.com.au (secondary, medium confidence) as the official site's full spec table was not directly extracted. A facelifted Megane E-Tech (new 67kWh LFP battery, up to 500km WLTP, 164kW motor) is confirmed by press reports for an Australian launch in H1 2027; it is included as a separate 'announced' row with only the confirmed battery/range/power figures populated and price/other fields left null, since it is not yet orderable. Kangoo E-Tech van price could not be confirmed from any source and is left null rather than guessed. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): Renault's own Kangoo E-Tech page makes no mention of V2L/vehicle-to-load, and no reviewer coverage found claims otherwise; v2l set to false and flagged low-confidence (absence-of-evidence).

Skoda AU BEV lineup (Sept 2026) uses the plain 'Enyaq' and 'Elroq' naming (no 'iV' suffix). Enyaq range: Select 60, Sportline 85, Coupe Sportline 85, RS and Coupe RS (MY27 spec sheet, all currently orderable). Elroq range: Select 60, Select 85 and 130 Years Edition currently orderable; an Elroq Sportline variant is confirmed for Australia with orders opening October 2026 but final specs/price were not yet published at time of research, so it is listed as 'announced' with most fields null. An 'Elroq RS' was reported by AU motoring press (Chasing Cars) with only an estimated/TBC price and is therefore omitted as unconfirmed. Skoda's official spec sheets/pages publish only drive-away pricing (MRDP); priceAud values below are the 'before on-road costs' MSRP figures reported by CarExpert/Chasing Cars (secondary sources), so priceAud is marked low-confidence with fieldSources citing those articles. RS variants report a split front/rear torque figure (e.g. 134Nm front / 545Nm rear) that cannot be validly summed into a single torqueNm value, so torqueNm is null for RS variants. Elroq 130 Years Edition range/consumption and DC charge rate were sourced from an older MY26-dated Skoda spec document and a 2025 CarExpert article rather than the current MY27 sheet, so those fields are marked low-confidence.

brands.publisher: EV Automotive (ev-a.com.au) - independent Australian importer/distributor of Skywell vans
brands.notes: V2L (Sept 2026 pass): no V2L/V2X capability found for the EC11 in any manufacturer or press material reviewed (importer spec sheet, CarsGuide, AEVA-derived light-commercial fact sheet summaries); v2l set to false for both E-Cargo and E-Crew and flagged low-confidence given the sparse documentation for this independently-imported model. Skywell IS genuinely sold new in Australia, but only as a single model, the EC11 electric van (in E-Cargo and E-Crew body variants), imported and distributed by an independent Australian importer, EV Automotive (ev-a.com.au), rather than by a Skywell-badged factory-backed distributor. This is corroborated by multiple independent commercial channels: fleetplan.com.au and easifleet.com.au both list the EC11 as a current new/novated-lease vehicle in 2026, and carsales.com.au / carsguide.com.au / drive.com.au all carry EC11 research/showroom pages. No other Skywell model (e.g. BE11, EV9, ET5) was found confirmed as on sale new in Australia as of Sept 2026 - the EC11 is the only current Skywell nameplate in market. Pricing is genuinely unclear/unverifiable: Drive.com.au's showroom page lists a 2025 E-Cargo RWD at $59,990 (MRLP, GST-inclusive, excl. on-roads), while CarsGuide cites third-party (Glass's Information Services) pricing of $89,990-$120,000 for the 2026 range, and carsales.com.au's own research pages say price is simply 'not available' for both the E-Cargo and E-Crew. EV Automotive's own official site (ev-a.com.au) does not publish a price at all. Given this scale of disagreement across sources (a >$30k spread) and the complete absence of a price on the importer's own site, priceAud is recorded as null for both variants rather than guessed. Technical specifications for the E-Cargo variant are well documented on ev-a.com.au's own specification table and are used directly; the E-Crew (12-seat people-mover) variant shares the same underlying platform/powertrain per Drive.com.au and BitAuto but EV Automotive's site does not carry a dedicated detailed spec sheet for it, so several E-Crew fields are recorded as null pending a dedicated spec page.

smart is confirmed actively sold in Australia as of September 2026 via the official au.smart.com site, which lists two current model lines: smart #1 and smart #3 (both Geely-Mercedes-Benz-joint-venture BEVs), each with three trims (Pro+, Premium, BRABUS). smart #1 data below was extracted directly from the official smart.com/au configurator/model pages (primary source). smart #3 official model page did not expose a full technical-data table in scrapeable form, so smart #3 specs are corroborated from AU motoring press (carsorted.ai, CarExpert, carsales) and are lower confidence overall. Two systematic gaps: (1) the smart #1 official page states 200kW only for the Premium trim and 315kW for BRABUS, without repeating the figure for Pro+; real-world knowledge suggests Pro+ shares Premium's powertrain, but per the no-invention rule this is left null and flagged rather than assumed. (2) Battery usable capacity for smart #3 could not be confirmed on any AU source reviewed; left null. Pricing for smart #1 is the official RRP before on-road costs; pricing for smart #3 is sourced from press (some of which quote drive-away pricing rather than MSRP) and is flagged accordingly. Torque figures for higher-power / dual-motor variants (smart #1 BRABUS, smart #3 BRABUS) are ambiguous in sources (single motor vs combined system torque are not always distinguished) and are flagged low-confidence or left null rather than risk conflating a single-motor spec with a combined system figure.

Solterra facelift (MY26) confirmed directly via Subaru Australia's official model page plus a detailed CarExpert pricing/specs article and review. The facelift shares its 74.7kWh battery and 150kW DC charging with its Toyota bZ4X platform-twin. Peak system torque for the base AWD grade is officially unquoted by Subaru/CarExpert ('TBC') and is left null rather than reusing the previous-generation 337Nm figure.

Model S and Model X confirmed no longer orderable in Australia (CarExpert: 'Tesla Australia currently sells the Model 3 sedan and Model Y SUV. The Model S and Model X are no longer part of the local new-vehicle range.'). Prices extracted directly from Tesla AU configurator via browser (before on-road costs). Model Y L confirmed as 6-seat variant per CarExpert. Battery kWh for Model Y L marked uncertain — browser AI extracted 75kWh but 600km WLTP at that capacity seems optimistic; flagged as lowConfidenceField. Tesla does not offer V2L on any current AU models. Consumption figures not published by Tesla AU configurator; set to null.

bZ4X 2WD and AWD specs and pricing directly confirmed via Toyota Australia's official spec PDF (dated June 2026) and CarExpert's December 2025 pricing article for the updated MY26 range (both variants now share a 74.7kWh battery, up from the original 71.4kWh). The bZ4X Touring AWD (280kW flagship grade) is confirmed via the official toyota.com.au page but its driveaway price is listed as 'currently unavailable' on Toyota's own site, so priceAud is left null rather than guessed. Toyota hybrids and the Mirai FCEV are out of scope and excluded.

Only BEV models in current AU lineup are ID.4, ID.5 and ID.Buzz (incl. ID.Buzz Cargo commercial van). ID.3 and ID.7 are NOT sold in Australia (ID.7 has been repeatedly ruled out by VW Australia spokespeople in press statements from 2023 through 2026, citing focus on the electric SUV range). VW Australia's own model pages predominantly advertise driveaway campaign pricing rather than MSRP before on-road costs; priceAud below uses the manufacturer list price (before on-road costs) as reported in VW's own price-cut announcements and corroborated by CarExpert/GoAuto/CarsGuide, per each variant's priceBasis field. Several ID.Buzz technical figures (GTX torque: 590Nm per CarExpert vs 560Nm per CarsGuide; Pro LWB power: 210kW assumed vs a conflicting 120kW figure in one CarsGuide table; AC charge rate assumed at VW's standard 11kW where not separately confirmed; towing capacity for ID.5 assumed identical to the equivalent-drivetrain ID.4 per AEVA, and largely unpublished for ID.Buzz Pro/GTX variants) show conflicts across secondary sources or were not published by VW Australia at all; these are flagged per-variant in lowConfidenceFields. VW's AEVA fact sheet confirms the ID.4 (and by extension the MEB-based ID.5) has no V2X/V2L capability in the Australian market, despite one aggregator (evdbau) claiming V2L support for the ID.5 -- the AEVA figure was preferred as the more EV-specialist, dated source. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): all four ID.Buzz variants (same MEB platform as ID.4/ID.5) previously had v2l left null; VW Commercial Vehicles has announced a 2.0kW V2L function arriving via a 'Summer 2026' software update, but reporting is explicit that this rollout is currently Europe/UK-only with no confirmed Australian timing, so the current AU-market ID.Buzz (incl. Cargo) is set to v2l:false, flagged low-confidence pending confirmation of if/when the update reaches Australia.

Volvo AU's own EX30/EX90 spec pages label the consumption figure as 'NEDC' even though Volvo AU markets its range figures elsewhere as WLTP; this looks like a site labelling artefact rather than a genuine NEDC test, so rangeCycle is recorded as null for EX30/EX90 rather than guessed. The dedicated EC40 specifications sub-page returned 404 at fetch time, so EC40 numeric specs (battery, power, range) could not be confirmed from the primary source; only a price figure from a secondary source (CarsGuide) is included, flagged low-confidence. Community-sourced ev-wiki.org mentions of an 'ES90' for Volvo Australia was NOT corroborated by any official or reputable press source and has been excluded entirely rather than included as a speculative row. EX40 (the renamed XC40 Recharge — previously wrongly excluded from this file as an unconfirmed 'community-sourced' claim; it is in fact a genuine, currently-sold model) has now been added. Its /specifications/ sub-page returned 403 at fetch time, so EX40 figures below are press-sourced (CarExpert, thebeep) rather than manufacturer-confirmed, and are flagged low-confidence accordingly. Press sources disagreed materially on price by ~$5,000-13,000 depending on state/promo/drive-away timing; the figures used here come from CarExpert's 2026-03-31 report of a $7,000 national MSRP price cut, which is the most specific and recent single data point found. PRICE AND SPEC CORRECTIONS (Sept 2026 pass): volvocars.com.au's own /specifications/ pages for EX30 and EX90 return 403 to automated fetches (Volvo's own bot-blocking, not a client-side network/VPN issue — confirmed by retrying after ruling out a local Cloudflare WARP/DNS cause), so this pass is press-sourced. EX30 priceAud filled from CarExpert's dedicated Plus/Ultra spec pages and its EX30 Cross Country pricing article, which gives a clean one-page table of all four current EX30 configurations. EX90 priceAud filled from a Chasing Cars review giving both Plus ($124,990) and Ultra Performance ($134,990) prices with matching power/torque figures. While researching EX90 pricing, multiple independent sources (CarsGuide's own Plus Twin Motor spec page, thebeep.com.au, Chasing Cars, general press) consistently gave power/torque/range/0-100 figures materially different from what this file previously recorded (300kW/770Nm/5.9s for Twin Motor vs the previous 330kW/670Nm/5.5s; 380kW/910Nm/4.9s for Twin Motor Performance vs the previous 500kW/870Nm/4.2s; 570km WLTP for both vs the previous 521km) — these look like a genuine prior data error rather than a source disagreement, since every current source agrees with each other and disagrees with the old figures, so they have been corrected rather than left as a documented conflict. EX30's existing power/torque/battery/range figures were re-checked against CarExpert's dedicated Plus/Ultra spec pages during this pass and found to match exactly (200kW/343Nm/69kWh gross/64kWh usable/462km WLTP for Single Motor Extended Range), so those fields were left unchanged.

brands.publisher: XPENG ANZ (XPeng Australia and New Zealand)
brands.notes: XPENG launched in Australia in late 2024 via distributor TrueEV. Factory-backed XPeng ANZ (XPeng Australia and New Zealand) took over distribution in April 2026; TrueEV and XPeng are in Federal Court proceedings. XPeng ANZ is currently selling: (1) the updated G6 (referred to as 'New G6' or 2027 MY in some press, arriving in AU showrooms July 2026) in four variants; and (2) the X9 electric people mover (available to order July 2026, deliveries commencing shortly after). While the X9 is sold as an EREV in China, Australia receives BEV-only versions — no EREV exclusion required for X9. The L03 BEV and G9L BEV are confirmed for AU launch in Q4 2026 (October–December) but not yet orderable as of September 2026; they are included as 'announced'. The L03 also has an EREV version; only BEV is listed here. The G9L will offer both EV and EREV in AU; only BEV listed. The L05 is scheduled for January 2027 and is not included. Note: the xpeng.com.au/g6-specification page as indexed appears to show the outgoing 2024 G6 (190 kW, 66 kWh, 435 km WLTP); the current 'New G6' specs are sourced from the store.xpeng.com/au configurator. Towing capacity for G6 and X9 is not confirmed in AU specifications reviewed. G6 segment is 'suv-small' per GoAuto press categorisation ('Small SUV over $45K segment').

brands.publisher: CarExpert.com.au, Drive.com.au, thebeep.com.au (no standalone zeekr.com.au confirmed; vehicles sold through Zeekr Australia network)
brands.notes: Zeekr is firmly established in Australia as of September 2026 with three BEV model lines: Zeekr X (small SUV), Zeekr 7X (medium SUV), and Zeekr 009 (people-mover/MPV). All are orderable through the Zeekr Australia dealer network. The 2026 Zeekr X launched in Australian showrooms from May 2026 with national drive-away pricing. The 7X has been on sale since 2025. The 009 FWD grade was added in November 2025. The 8X and 9X announced for late 2026/early 2027 are PHEV/EREV (not BEV) and are therefore excluded from this file. The 7GT electric wagon was mentioned as under consideration for AU launch but is not confirmed as orderable and is excluded. Prices for the 7X are drive-away from thebeep.com.au (aggregated from Zeekr Australia); 009 prices are before on-road costs per Drive.com.au. VFACTS/EVC sales data confirms real AU volumes: Zeekr X 665 total 2025 sales, 142 YTD 2026; Zeekr 009 123 total 2025 sales, 97 YTD 2026; Zeekr 7X 2,698 units Jan-Apr 2026.

emptyBrands.notes: WITHDRAWN FROM MARKET: Citroen Australia (importer Inchcape) formally ceased all new-vehicle sales in Australia effective 1 November 2024, ending a 101+ year presence, after sales collapsed to just 87 units in H1 2024 (down 35% year-on-year, versus a 2007 peak of 3803 annual deliveries). Existing orders placed before 1 November 2024 were fulfilled, and Citroen's ~35 dealer network transitioned to a service-and-maintenance-only operation; the importer refocused on its sibling brand Peugeot. At the time of withdrawal Citroen's Australian range was petrol/diesel only (C3, C4, C5 Aircross, C5 X) -- no BEV was part of the final local lineup. Search results also surfaced ccarprice.com listings claiming current Australian availability and pricing for an e-C4 X, e-Berlingo and e-SpaceTourer; ccarprice.com is a low-reliability, seemingly auto-generated aggregator that explicitly disclaims guaranteed accuracy, and its claims directly conflict with the official Citroen Australia market-exit announcement and multiple corroborating reputable press sources (carsales, WhichCar, Drive, CarExpert), so those listings are treated as incorrect/not credible and excluded. As of September 2026, Citroen sells no new vehicles of any powertrain in Australia, BEV or otherwise.

Foton's current Australian passenger/light-commercial lineup (Tunland V7 and Tunland V9 utes, priced approx. $39,990-$49,990) is confirmed across multiple 2025/2026 sources to be diesel or diesel mild-hybrid only, with no battery-electric variant offered new in Australia. No evidence was found this session of an on-sale Foton or Foton-affiliated (e.g. 'Asiastar') BEV in the Australian market; a prior research pass had flagged a possible 'Tunland G7 EV' but this could not be corroborated this session against any dealer, press, or manufacturer source and is treated as unconfirmed/likely incorrect. Foton does sell electric light trucks/buses in some overseas markets, but none were verified as available for retail new-vehicle purchase in Australia within the 4.5-tonne GVM passenger/LCV scope of this dataset.

Isuzu does not currently sell a battery-electric vehicle in Australia as of September 2026. The Isuzu D-Max EV (battery-electric dual-cab ute) has been confirmed by Isuzu as planned for the Australian market, and has appeared in various global/regional launches, but multiple 2025 reports indicate no confirmed Australian on-sale date, with local timing reportedly linked to New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES) policy settings and light commercial vehicle CO2 targets. No Isuzu BEV is currently orderable new in Australia.

REAL DOUBT / LIKELY WITHDRAWN: Jaguar's I-Pace was, as of a November 2024 review, sellable in Australia on remaining stock only ('sufficient stock... to carry us through to 2025'), following JLR's July 2024 global decision to axe the I-Pace and E-Pace as 'zero-profitability products'. CarExpert's own 2026 I-Pace pricing page (published 20 Aug 2026) shows 'Price not available' and zero year-to-date sales for 2026, and the official jaguar.com/en-au I-Pace specifications page itself returned a broken/unavailable content block at fetch time. Given no confirmed current price, zero 2026 sales, and a global discontinuation decision from mid-2024, the I-Pace is judged to be effectively no longer orderable new in Australia as of September 2026 and is therefore NOT listed as a current variant (an empty variants array is used) rather than assumed still on sale. Note also: a March 2026 CarExpert report described a recall affecting ~270 older (2017-2021 build) I-Pace units for a battery overheating/fire risk, capping charging at 90% pending a permanent fix -- this affects existing fleet vehicles, not new-vehicle orderability, and is unrelated to the withdrawal finding above. No other Jaguar BEV (e.g. a Jaguar 'Type 00' successor GT) has been confirmed as launched or orderable in Australia.

Mahindra Australia sells ZERO battery-electric vehicles as of September 2026. The current retail lineup is exclusively internal-combustion: Scorpio (diesel), XUV3XO (petrol), XUV700 (petrol/diesel), plus an upcoming diesel-only Lifestyler dual-cab ute - none of these are electrified. AU press (carsales.com.au, 2026-09-02; Drive.com.au, 2026-09-02; GoAuto, 2026-08-18) reports Mahindra is evaluating a trio of EVs (XEV 9e, XEV 9S, BE 6) for possible future Australian launch - a single XEV 9e demonstrator has been imported on temporary plates for internal dealer display, and Australian trademark filings exist for 'XEV 9E' and 'BE 6' - but none has a confirmed launch date, Australian specification, or pricing. This does not meet the bar for 'announced' status (which requires a confirmed AU launch), so no variants are listed. Revisit this brand as these EVs progress toward a firm Australian launch commitment.

Ram does not currently sell any battery-electric vehicle in Australia as of September 2026. The Ram 1500 REV, a planned full-BEV version of the Ram 1500, was cancelled by Stellantis/RAM globally in September 2025 before reaching an Australian right-hand-drive conversion or launch. The Ram Ramcharger (an extended-range electric vehicle / EREV with a petrol generator providing extended range) is out of scope for this dataset because it is not a pure battery-electric vehicle. No other Ram BEV model is confirmed for the Australian market.
